newsitem.title: UK: World coffee producers, consumers debate state of market.
newsitem.headline: World coffee producers, consumers debate state of market.

text.p: Coffee producers and consumers on Tuesday differed over an International Coffee Organization (ICO) document reviewing the market situation and stressing in particular recent volatility and price slides, delegates said.
"Producers and consumers are split over the need for a document on the market situation," said one ICO delegate.

The ICO, which groups 58 of the world's consumers and producers, is holding Executive meetings this week. The document, drafted by the ICO's economist and presented to its Executive Board on Tuesday, also estimated 1996/97 world coffee production at 99.7 million 60-kg bags against 85.6 million in the 1995/96 period, delegates said.
But 1996/97 consumption and export forecasts were not included by the ICO.
"The document is a review of what has happened in the market over the last few months," said ICO spokesman Pablo Dubois.
Delegates said the document stressed "in particular" recent price slides and the market's volatility during the May to September period.
Robusta coffee futures, which hit near ten-year highs of $4,140 a tonne in August 1994, were down in May at $1,970 a tonne. But this week they dipped to more than two-year lows of $1,475 a tonne.
The ICO document blamed price slides on investment funds which liquidated positions despite improved consumption prospects and bad growing weather in Central and South America.
Further pressure, according to the ICO, came when long-holders sold off their positions in 1996 as frost in Brazil, the world's largest grower, failed to materialise.
But traders said the sell off also follows forecasts for higher world 1996/97 output, led mainly by Brazil where output should recover after frosts and drought in 1994.

While some producer delegates are against the ICO reviewing the market situation, which they say would be best left to forecasting and trading bodies, some consumers see the role of the ICO in providing statistics and reviews as key.
"The ICO, as an international commodity body, should welcome such a chance (to review market situation)," said one consumer delegate.
During the ICO's May meeting, an official ICO document on the market situation was not issued to delegates.

In other business, the ICO's Finance Committee on Tuesday approved the draft administrative budget for 1996/97, said delegates, adding that a project to develop gourmet coffee potential was due to be signed on Thursday after being approved by the UN's Common Fund for Commodities.
The gourmet project will enable five coffee-producers, including three African ones, to implement sustainable gourmet quality development and marketing strategies.

Another project, backed by the ICO, which aims to control the spread of coffee berry borer, has been approved by the Fund's Consultative Committee and the next step is for it to be approved by the Fund's executive board.
On Wednesday, the ICO Executive Board will be briefed by a scientist from the International Mycological Institute on coffee wilt disease in Zaire.

Also, an official from the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) will brief the ICO on the new merger between LIFFE and the London Commodity Exchange (LCE), said delegates.
